_: The one place PocketAgent's colour and icon geometry are written down. tools/make_brand.py reads this and emits every derived asset; tests/brand-assets-test.py reads it and refuses anything that drifted. Editing a colour here and running the generator is the whole procedure -- there is no second place to remember.

brand._: Deep teal. Chosen against the four agents this app hosts so the mark is never mistaken for one of them: Claude is terracotta, Codex and Cursor are monochrome, Antigravity is blue-violet. It is also clear of the three colours that mean something inside the app (green added, amber needs-you, red removed), so brand colour and status colour can never be confused.

neutral._: Warm, not grey. The interface is deliberately neutral: buttons and links are ink on cream and bone on ink, so that every coloured pixel in the app is carrying meaning rather than decoration.

semantic._: The only other colours in the app, and each one means exactly one thing.

geometry._: The mark on a 512 artboard: two brackets around a four-point spark. Every derived size is this artboard scaled, so the proportions never drift between the launcher, the splash and the notification.

desktop._: The Ubuntu desktop inside the container arrived with a navy palette inherited from the app this one grew out of. Rather than pin a list of replacements that would go stale, the rule is stated here and enforced by tests/brand-assets-test.py: no colour in the desktop scripts may sit in the azure-to-violet band, which is where every one of those navies lived and where the brand's own teal (186 degrees) never goes. The one exception is the terminal's ANSI palette, which is a convention every program on the system relies on and is not ours to re-tint.
